ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct FINTRAC-compliant client due diligence and mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) assessment for foreign and domestic PEPs. Screen all directors, officers, and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, and the UK HM Treasury consolidated list. Verify beneficial ownership through the confidential provincial transparency register and document all screening outputs in the corporate legal file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online — Name Request Service (Corporate Registry, Government of British Columbia)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted using Latin alphabet characters, numerals, and accepted punctuation marks. English and French forms are permitted for word elements; distinctive, descriptive, and legal element components must be recognizable and pronounceable in the English or French language. Transliteration into Latin script is required for any non-Latin script; the registered name must match the transliteration exactly.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation cannot be extended after 56 days; the applicant must submit a new name request. If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, providing legal argument and any supporting evidence to rebut the confusing-similarity or prohibited-word grounds. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia, or simply reserve an alternative name through the Corporate Online portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible only where it provides a physical street address located in British Columbia capable of accepting registered service, maintaining corporate records, and generating physical business records on demand. A purely mail-forwarding or non-physical virtual address is impermissible. The industry is non-licensed, so this arrangement is commercially acceptable for an ASO/SEO localization agency.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified at less than 5% probability in any given compliance year for a non-licensed low-risk industry, although unannounced verification visits may occur during a Canada Revenue Agency audit or a Companies Office compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, Part 2 (ss. 4-13) — Incorporation; s. 18 (registered office), s. 51 (share subscription and consideration), s. 173 (annual reports)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) together with Notice of Articles (Form 2) and Articles (Form 3) filed under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) and the Business Corporations Act Forms Regulation, B.C. Reg. 532/2004
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under British Columbia law. A BC business corporation may be incorporated without initial capital; shares may be issued at any time for any lawful consideration fixed by the directors under s. 51 of the Business Corporations Act. The authorized share structure is set out in the Notice of Articles and Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED THAT:
1. The incorporation of the Company under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) is ratified; the Articles and Notice of Articles filed with the Registry are adopted as the constating documents.
2. The registered and records office shown in the Notice of Articles is confirmed, and the directors named therein are appointed to hold office.
3. The directors are authorized to allot and issue common shares to the subscribers at the consideration fixed by the board.
4. The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer/President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer/Treasurer, with customary authority.
5. The officers are directed to open corporate bank accounts, procure insurance, and complete all Registry and CRA filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Name Approval application via Corporate Online (NUANS-assisted search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an NUANS name search through a BC Registry service provider or submit an online Name Approval Request via Corporate Online. Select a distinctive corporate name containing a legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'). If no name is required, proceed directly to a numbered company incorporation to avoid delay. Retain the name approval number for inclusion in the incorporation application; the approval remains valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (English and/or French)
NUANS name search report (for non-numbered companies)
Name Approval Request receipt and payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, amend the name by adding distinguishing elements or altering the legal element and resubmit within the validity window; alternatively, incorporate immediately as a numbered company and apply for a name change after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign the Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2) (stating the registered office, records office, authorized share structure, and first directors), and Articles (Form 3). Submit the package electronically through Corporate Online, pay the CAD $350 digital filing fee by credit card or electronic payment, and certify director consents. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Incorporation Application (Form 1)
Notice of Articles (Form 2) including registered office address and director names
Articles (Form 3) — standard or special articles
Name approval number (where a named company is incorporated)
Directors' Consent to Act as Directors (Form 4 or electronic consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the application for correction, revise the identified fields (e.g., registered office address, share structure, director consent) and resubmit through Corporate Online; the Certificate of Incorporation will be dated as of the successful re-filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Registry Profile Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry — BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and archive the Certificate of Incorporation and endorsed Notice of Articles from the Corporate Online account. Activate the BC Registry corporate profile, confirm the records office address, and calendar the annual report deadline (two months after each anniversary of incorporation). Arrange corporate records book, share certificates, and minute book in accordance with Part 5 of the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered Notice of Articles
Corporate Online BC Registry profile credentials
Corporate records book and minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For clerical errors in the certificate, file a corrected application with the Registrar; for registry data errors, file the applicable Notice of Change through Corporate Online to rectify the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and open CRA program accounts: Corporation Income Tax (RC account), GST/HST (RT account) where annual worldwide taxable revenue exceeds the CAD $30,000 registration threshold, and Payroll Deductions (RP account) if hiring employees. Nominate a director or officer as the authorized representative and confirm the registered office as the mailing address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered Notice of Articles
Government-issued identification for the authorizing officer/director
Registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried, reconcile the legal name and incorporation number with the BC Registry record and resubmit; contact CRA Business Enquiries (1-800-959-5525) to correct duplicate or incomplete program account registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Workplace Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or applicable British Columbia municipal licensing authority); WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general municipal business licence classifying the activity as 'Business and Administrative Services — Advertising and Digital Marketing' at the leased office location. Confirm the premises comply with municipal zoning and the BC Building Code occupancy requirements. Register the employer with WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety coverage before any staff commence work.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Lease agreement or proof of premises occupancy
Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
WorkSafeBC employer registration form
Fire safety and occupancy approval for the leased space
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is withheld due to zoning or occupancy non-conformity, apply for a development variance permit or relocation approval, or secure compliant premises; reapply with the corrected documentation and full disclosure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board governs digital advertising, app store optimization, or SEO localization services in British Columbia; the activity is classified as an office-based professional service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no provincial industrial operating or manufacturing permit applies; a municipal general business licence is the only operational authorization required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical industrial facility, no emissions source, and no reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act; office-based digital services do not trigger an EIA designation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the agency has no wastewater, VOC, or process emissions; the business is subject only to municipal solid waste diversion, recycling obligations under the BC Recycling Regulation, and landlord-imposed building HVAC and water usage standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy and fire safety approval for the leased office issued by the local fire authority under the BC Fire Code; structural load and Building Code Part 3 compliance confirmed by the municipal building inspector for the commercial premises; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and clearance for the employer; municipal business licence confirming zoning and use compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal corporate income tax and GST/HST; British Columbia Ministry of Finance for BC provincial income tax and Provincial Sales Tax (PST). Primary portals: CRA My Business Account and BC eTaxBC / BC Corporate Online.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned BC corporation must first be incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or registered as an extra-provincial company under the BC Business Corporations Act. It must then obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) through CRA’s Business Registration Online service or Form RC1, and activate the GST/HST and corporate income tax program accounts. If the corporation will make PST-taxable sales in British Columbia, a separate BC PST registration is required through eTaxBC. Non-resident ownership is permitted; no minimum capitalization or Canadian director residency is required for this entity structure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A Canadian-incorporated BC corporation is a resident corporation subject to federal and BC corporate income tax on worldwide income. No entity-classification election is available at the federal or provincial level. Hybrid mismatch and excessive interest-financing rules in the Income Tax Act apply automatically, including restrictions designed to neutralize reverse-hybrid structures and double-dip deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) federal value-added tax plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST). BC does not participate in the HST; therefore, the federal 5% GST and the separate BC PST apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. A non-resident carrying on business in Canada that makes taxable supplies must register for GST/HST when worldwide GST/HST taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. BC PST registration has no general turnover threshold and becomes mandatory as soon as the business makes PST-taxable sales in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API invoice clearance. GST/HST invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form provided they satisfy the disclosure requirements in the Excise Tax Act. CRA is implementing voluntary PEPPOL-based e-invoicing and EDI channels for public procurement, but there is no statutory requirement for a private SEO/ASO agency to obtain pre-approval or digital stamping on invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: SEO/ASO localization services supplied to a non-resident client may be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. The agency must show that the recipient is a non-resident, the recipient is not GST/HST-registered in respect of the supply, and the service is not rooted in Canadian real property or tangible personal property. Services performed in Canada for a client located abroad generally qualify when the client does not receive the benefit through a Canadian business. If the recipient is a registered GST/HST person, the supply generally becomes taxable at 5% GST unless another specific zero-rating provision applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No customs export declaration is required for intangible digital services; CRA substantiation relies on the executed client agreement, itemized invoices, and contemporaneous proof that the recipient is a non-resident such as a foreign corporate registry extract, exchange of information certificate, or other statutory residency declaration.
Bank statements, SWIFT confirmations, or Wise/Payoneer settlement records evidencing receipt of foreign currency into the Canadian corporate bank account and traceability to the exported service.

For any ancillary physical goods shipped from Canada, the standard export package would include Form B3-3 Canada Customs Coding Form or equivalent electronic export declaration, commercial invoice, packing slip, bill of lading or airway bill, and payment evidence; this component is inapplicable to pure digital ASO and SEO services.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Insufficient export zero-rating substantiation permits CRA to reassess the supply as taxable at 5% GST/HST and to collect unpaid tax, daily statutory interest, and penalties. A negligent or fraudulent zero-rating claim can attract penalties of up to 25% of the tax assessed, and the normal four-year reassessment period is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is shown. CRA may also coordinate with the Canada Border Services Agency and foreign tax treaty partners to verify export proceeds, non-resident status, and banking flows; wilful evasion can result in prosecution and court-imposed fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); no separate foreign exchange administration for FX control purposes. Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) supervises AML/ATF compliance, and Global Affairs Canada administers economic sanctions and export controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both the current and capital account. There is no statutory requirement for central bank approval on capital inflows, dividend remittances, loan servicing, or profit repatriation. Funds may be freely converted to CAD or foreign currency at market rates; the only material fiscal hurdles are withholding taxes on distributions and corporate reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts; standard CRA tax filing, transfer-pricing documentation, and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting requirements still apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating account in CAD/USD; escrow/subscription account available if required
Operating account with cross-border treasury platform and USD clearing
Operating account; international trade desk and multi-currency account options
Operating account; global banking and foreign currency settlement services
Operating account; US-dollar cross-border banking solutions
Operating account; regional mid-market commercial banking and escrow services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is High for using Wise Business, Payoneer, and comparable regulated non-bank payment service providers as secondary disbursement and collection rails. These entities are not authorized Canadian banks and do not offer CDIC deposit insurance; their Canadian activity is permitted only through FINTRAC-registered money services business arrangements or equivalent exemption. EMIs domiciled in the EU/UK can lawfully assist cross-border treasury operations but cannot be relied upon as the primary corporate bank account for statutory corporate purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal legal requirement requires directors to appear physically at a bank branch in British Columbia. Schedule I banks generally permit remote onboarding through digital identity verification and video KYC interviews. For non-resident directors and substantial beneficial owners, banks commonly require: certified passport copies, notarized proof of address, a Canadian registered agent or service address, and a remote video interview; physical attendance may be triggered only in exceptional AML risk cases. Federal FINTRAC CDD rules are satisfied through reliable independent identity documentation rather than in-person presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered address is a virtual office or service address without physical operating premises in Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or shared-office service agreement, utility or internet bill, BC Registry listing, corporate website operational proof, and a local address verification declaration signed by the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign ownership or directors resident in a jurisdiction perceived as higher AML/CFT risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, tax residency certificates, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, corporate organizational chart, register of directors and shareholders, and documented commercial substance in British Columbia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border digital-marketing revenues from unregulated app developers without detailed service documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client agreements, app ownership evidence from App Store Connect and Google Play Console, monthly ASO and localization deliverable reports, itemized invoices, and platform performance analytics corresponding to invoiced amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material inbound wire transfers from third-party payment aggregators or non-counterparty sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete reconciliation ledger matching each wire to client invoices, underlying client authorization of payment, signed service contracts, a project timeline with deliverables, and a formal source-of-funds explanation acceptable to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid or high-frequency disbursement pattern inconsistent with stated agency business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast, historical profit and loss statements, CRA income tax filings, bank statements showing continuity, contractor/service-provider agreements, and a written narrative explaining industry seasonality and geographic client mix.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions or shareholder loans must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the investing shareholder's licensed banking institution to the British Columbia corporation's Schedule I operating account. The remittance message should include in field 70 a precise purpose narrative such as 'Shareholder equity injection' or 'Shareholder loan per loan agreement dated [date]' and reference the applicable corporate resolution. Bank compliance expects a board resolution, updated share register or loan agreement, source-of-wealth documents, and a beneficial-ownership declaration. There is no Canadian exchange-control approval, but Statistics Canada may require balance-of-payments reporting for foreign direct investment; OFAC screening applies to any USD correspondent leg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for an app-growth agency are service payments, not physical trade, so SWIFT MT103 wire transfers are the primary clearing rail for international vendors exceeding material thresholds. For recurring low-value disbursements, Wise Business and Payoneer can serve as efficient faster-payment rails; domestic Canadian payments are cleared through EFT/Interac. Commercial letters of credit have no practical application to intangible agency services. Every disbursement must include contract or purchase-order references in MT103 field 70, and the corporation should maintain a full audit trail to satisfy FINTRAC record-keeping and CRA expense substantiation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable spot and forward contracts in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP with a Canadian chartered bank under a standard ISDA/CSA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging exotics or emerging-market currency receivables where no deliverable forward market exists; legal in Canada but unnecessary for G10 currencies
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term shareholder loans or intercompany financing exposures
Currency options and collars on a case-by-case basis for committed multi-year service contracts if bank documentation and board authorization support the hedge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: British Columbia Corporate Annual Report (including Significant Individuals Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation every year (e.g., incorporation anniversary 15-Mar -> due 15-May)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 30.00; failure to file for two consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off under s. 274 of the Business Corporations Act (BCBCA).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (even for nil return); balance due generally 2 months after year-end for CCPCs, or 3 months for non-CCPCs (subject to instalment requirements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeat failure within 3 years triggers 10% penalty; daily compounding interest applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the end of the GST/HST reporting period (typically fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the net tax owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (or a $250 minimum where applicable), plus daily compound interest under the Excise Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset/revenue threshold under BCBCA. A private business corporation must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders waive the appointment by unanimous written consent (s. 204/205 BCBCA). Mandatory audit is required for reporting issuers (publicly traded companies) and where shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares exercise their statutory audit request rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private enterprises may prepare annual financial statements under Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) or IFRS; reporting issuers must use IFRS per National Instrument 52-107. The T2 income tax return uses taxable income under the Income Tax Act, reconciling to the accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Effective for all BC private companies, the transparent ownership register must report every individual with significant control (ISC - holding 25%+ of votes, 25%+ fair market value, or influential interest). Share transfers must be recorded in the register of members within 12 days after the company receives notice; any resulting ISC register changes must be recorded within 12 days. The annual report to the BC Registrar includes a mandatory Significant Individuals Report confirming the ISC register is current as of the filing date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (Transparent Ownership Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100-250 per year for a BC registered office and records office with mail scanning and compliance reminders
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-8,000 for a typical private agency (if audit is not waived); review engagements typically USD 1,500-3,000
